authorship.statement: Synthetic, renamed cards and rule text written by the implementing AI. Not independent, not expert-reviewed, not held out; gold values are the author's reading of the supplied text and may be wrong.

vocabulary.scope: fact kind for printed unconditional abilities (activated|triggered|spell|rule_definition); any other string names a scope v1 does not represent
vocabulary.trigger: ['<event>:<subject>'] of a triggered ability's trigger event
vocabulary.actor: sorted actors of the clause's effects in compiler vocabulary (self = this object, you = its controller); null = explicitly unjudged
vocabulary.finite_fuel: true when the clause consumes finite supplied fuel without renewal
vocabulary.output_events: sorted '<event>:<subject>' of the clause's effects. Effects outside the compiler's event vocabulary (pump, gain_keyword, counter, reveal, level_up, cast, return) use a descriptive token so an interpreted fact that omits or renames them scores wrong.
vocabulary.null: any non-scope dimension may be null: explicitly unjudged by the label author; reported as unjudged, never scored, and blocks all_scored_dimensions_correct

label_revisions.author: AI-authored (Claude Opus 5.5), same author as the original labels; not independent
label_revisions.reason: Scoring v1 never compared output events and ignored extracted dimensions with no gold key, so corrupted explore outputs left every score unchanged (alternate-provider review R1, P1).
label_revisions.added: output_events gold on all 40 labels, written from the quoted text, including effects the compiler vocabulary lacks (pump, gain_keyword, +1/+1 counter, reveal).

notes.explore actor: Ambiguous: the creature explores but the rule says its controller reveals and moves; compiler says you. Left null (explicitly unjudged) rather than adopting the compiler answer.
notes.explore zone_moves: The card clause itself moves no card; moves are labelled on the separate explore rule labels, consistent with the existing quantity gold.
notes.pump/flying actor: Changed [] to [self]: [] meant no compiler event outputs (grammar-informed); the text has an effect performed on this creature, matching the self convention for damage.
notes.reveal token: Revealing is a game action in the rule text; a reader could argue it is not an output event. It is included and contestable.
